name: discord-messaging-mcp
description: Discord (messaging): me, send, reply, list_inbound, get_thread. Every tool maps to a documented endp

platform_mcp_discord_bot_token.title: PLATFORM_MCP_DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN
platform_mcp_discord_bot_token.description: Bot token from the app's Bot page in the Developer Portal, pasted WITHOUT the 'Bot ' prefix: the runtime adds it and sends 'Authorization: Bot <token>' ('authentication is performed with the Authorization HTTP header in the format Authorization: TOKEN_TYPE TOKEN', https://docs.discord.com/developers/reference#authentication). Channel permissions needed: VIEW_CHANNEL + READ_MESSAGE_HISTORY (list_inbound, get_thread), SEND_MESSAGES (send, reply); the MESSAGE_CONTENT privileged intent to read other users' message content.

tools.name: me
tools.description: 'Returns the user object of the requester's account' — for a bot token the bot's own user (id, username, discriminator, global_name, bot: true).

tools.name: send
tools.description: `to` is a CHANNEL id (snowflake), not a user or address: 'Post a message to a guild text or DM channel' — to reach a user, first open a DM channel with POST /users/@me/channels (not offered) and pass that channel id. `text` is `content`, 'Message contents (up to 2000 characters)'; `subject` and `channel` are ignored. Needs SEND_MESSAGES in the channel. message_id is the created message's id.

tools.name: reply
tools.description: A Discord reply is a message carrying a message_reference to the parent: 'Replies are created by including a message_reference when sending a message. When sending, only message_id is required'. `thread_id` is that parent message id and `channel` (the channel the parent lives in) is REQUIRED — without it the runtime reports missing argument 'channel'. Needs READ_MESSAGE_HISTORY as well as SEND_MESSAGES ('The referenced message must exist and cannot be a system message').

tools.name: list_inbound
tools.description: Lists ONE channel: `channel` (a channel or thread id) is REQUIRED — bots have no cross-channel inbox endpoint (inbound push is the Gateway). 'Returns an array of message objects from newest to oldest'; Discord pages by message id (before / after / around), so `page` is ignored and only the newest `limit` (1-100, Discord default 50) messages are returned; `since` is not sent. 'If the current user is missing the READ_MESSAGE_HISTORY permission in the channel, then no messages will be returned', and other users' `content` is empty without the MESSAGE_CONTENT intent. `from` is author.id (username under raw.author); `thread_id` is the channel id; `sent_at` is the ISO-8601 `timestamp`.

tools.name: get_thread
tools.description: A Discord thread is itself a channel, so `thread_id` is the thread's channel id (a message's `thread.id`, or the id from a THREAD_CREATE event) and the same Get Channel Messages endpoint lists it; the vocabulary's `channel` is ignored. Same newest-first / id-cursor caveats as list_inbound (`page` ignored, newest `limit` messages only).
